title: Stair Climbing Workout: How to Do It at Home, in Your Apartment or at the Office
intro: Climbing stairs is free cardio that strengthens your legs and stamina without leaving home. If you live in an apartment or work in a multi-storey office, 10-15 minutes of stair climbing is already enough for one session.
muscles: Front thighs, back thighs, glutes and calves. Your heart and lungs also work hard.
steps: Wear shoes with good grip and hold the railing if needed.
Place your whole foot on the step, not just your toes.
Push through your heel, with your body leaning slightly forward.
Climb at a pace where you can still say short sentences.
Come down slowly, one step at a time, or take the lift down.
mistakes: Climbing on your toes only until your calves hurt quickly.
Knees caving inward when pushing up. Make sure your knees line up with your toes.
Rushing down the stairs. Going down puts more pressure on your knees.
easier: Do step-ups on the bottom step, 10 times on each leg. Or climb just 1-2 floors and rest when needed.
harder: Climb faster, add more floors or skip a step. You can also carry a backpack with water bottles for extra load.
dose: 10-15 minutes, 3 times a week. Example: climb 2-3 floors, come down slowly, repeat 4-6 times.
safety: Stop if you feel sharp knee pain, chest pain or dizziness. If you have heart or knee problems, get advice from a doctor or physio first.

faq.q: Can I climb up the stairs but take the lift down?
faq.a: Yes, it's actually good for beginners or people with sensitive knees. The climbing part is what trains your muscles and heart the most.

faq.q: Is climbing the office stairs every day enough?
faq.a: It adds very useful daily movement. If you can, add 2-3 short strength sessions a week and watch your food portions for more balanced results.

faq.q: Can climbing stairs slim down my thighs?
faq.a: Fat can't be removed from just one spot. Climbing stairs strengthens your thigh muscles, and when your eating and overall movement are under control, fat comes off slowly from your whole body, including your thighs.
